result:
Done. Final state: `bun run typecheck` passes, `bun test` passes (4 tests across 3 files, including the two I added), and `bunx guren check` reports 0 failures.

**What I changed**

Registration now hands the welcome email to the queue and returns as before. `app/Http/Controllers/Auth/RegisterController.ts` dispatches `SendWelcomeEmailJob` (new, `app/Jobs/`) after creating and signing in the user — a refused registration throws before that line, so it queues nothing. The job resolves the mail manager published for jobs and calls `sendWelcomeMail()` (`app/Mail/WelcomeMail.ts`), which sends from `MAIL_FROM_ADDRESS`/`MAIL_FROM_NAME` with subject `Welcome to <APP_NAME>, <name>!` and a plain-text greeting; a failed send throws so the queue retries. Neither subsystem existed yet, so I brought both up the way this project structures configuration — thin providers over `config/`: `config/queue.ts` maps `QUEUE_CONNECTION` to a driver (`sync` inline for dev, `memory`, `redis` for the production worker) and `config/mail.ts` maps `MAIL_MAILER` to a transport (`log`, `memory`, `resend`) plus the configured sender; `app/Providers/QueueProvider.ts` binds the queue manager, registers the job class so a worker can resolve a queued message back to it, and activates the configured driver, while `app/Providers/MailProvider.ts` binds the mail manager and publishes it globally for jobs (both leave a driver/manager installed before boot alone, so a test can point the app at its own queue and recording transport in either order). Both providers are registered in `src/app.ts`; `config/app.ts` gained `appName()`. Added `tests/RegisterController.test.ts` (registration redirects to `/dashboard`, sends nothing, leaves exactly one job waiting, and delivers exactly one correctly addressed message once a worker drains it; a refused registration leaves both empty), an ADR at `docs/adr/0002-queue-the-welcome-email.md`, and a short README note. I verified the development path end-to-end too: with `QUEUE_CONNECTION=sync`/`MAIL_MAILER=log` the message prints to the server output.
